title: Stress test: two concurrent worker lanes
description:
Operator-directed milestone, 2026-08-13: run two abacus dispatches at the same time and observe what breaks. Setup: at least two ready beads in the backlog, then two abacus run invocations launched concurrently (second starts while the first lane is still working). What the test exercises, each mapped to a prior fix: ab-iuf's main-tracker claim must make the second invocation select the SECOND bead, not re-dispatch the first — this is the primary assertion; two codex lanes work simultaneously in separate worktrees (no tree-claim coordination exists by design, worktrees are the isolation); both lanes close-before-push (zyb protocol), both open their own PRs (ab-yil), both get outcome-probed and reaped (zkq, wrq); the two lane branches' .beads close commits both conflict with the moving main tracker — ab-s1x's merge driver gets its first two-sided live test. Deliverable, per the abacus-geh pattern: record in this bead's notes the wall clock, both outcomes, and every deviation; file each failure worth fixing as its own bead. This bead depends on ab-iuf, ab-s1x, and ab-yil (operator ruling: after the existing backlog clears).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Two abacus run invocations launched concurrently with at least two ready beads.
- PASS requires all of: the second invocation selects the second bead (never re-dispatches the first); both lanes run simultaneously in separate worktrees; both beads end closed with two distinct lane branches and two distinct worker-opened PRs; both lanes outcome-probed and reaped by the engine; tracker merges auto-resolve via the merge driver.
- Alternatively the run FAILS with a deviation specific enough to act on, each failure filed as its own bead.
- Wall clock and both outcomes recorded in this bead's notes either way.
acceptance_criteria: Two abacus run invocations launched concurrently while at least two beads are ready. PASS requires all of: the second invocation selects the second bead (never re-dispatches the first — ab-iuf claim visible in the main tracker); both lanes run simultaneously in separate worktrees; both beads end closed with two distinct lane branches and two distinct worker-opened PRs; both lanes outcome-probed and reaped by the engine; tracker merges auto-resolve via the ab-s1x driver. Alternatively the run FAILS with a deviation specific enough to act on, recorded in notes with each failure filed as its own bead. Wall clock and both outcomes recorded in notes either way.

title: Reap tries clean removal first; force only as loud fallback
description:
src/main.rs line 206 area: the reap path passes --force to herdr worktree remove unconditionally for completed lanes. Post-zyb protocol a completed lane commits its bead close before pushing, so its worktree should always remove cleanly — unconditional force papers over the one signal that would catch a lane that violated the close-before-push protocol (the v8s lane needed force precisely because it stranded state; the zkq, zyb, wrq, iuf, s1x, lpk, yil lanes all removed clean).

Fix in the reap branch of cmd_run: attempt herdr worktree remove --workspace <id> WITHOUT --force; on failure whose stderr contains dirty_worktree_requires_force, print a loud warning naming the workspace and stating that a completed lane left uncommitted changes (protocol violation worth investigating), then retry with --force so the lane still reaps. Any other removal error propagates as today.

Worker note: run the full suite plus clippy and fmt before closing; open the PR per protocol.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the reap call in cmd_run (src/main.rs, the block passing --force around line 206) — force is unconditional.
2. Historical repro of the masked signal: the lane/abacus-v8s worktree removal was refused with error code dirty_worktree_requires_force until forced, because its bead close was stranded uncommitted (pre-zyb protocol).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Reap first attempts herdr worktree remove without --force.
- On dirty_worktree_requires_force it prints a warning naming the workspace and the protocol violation, then forces; other errors propagate unchanged.
- Unit test covers the dirty-detection predicate against the captured herdr error JSON.
- Full suite, clippy, fmt green; live validation on the next dispatched lane recorded in notes.

title: abacus run claims the selected bead in the main tracker before opening the lane
description: Observed 2026-08-13: abacus-zkq stayed open in the main tracker's br ready while its lane was mid-work, because the worker's claim lands only in the lane worktree's .beads copy — a second abacus run (sequential re-run today, concurrent lanes later) would re-dispatch the same bead. Fix in src/main.rs cmd_run: immediately after select_bead succeeds and before herdr worktree create, shell br update <bead-id> --claim in the target repo (same cwd as the br ready call). The claim lives in the main checkout's working tracker state; the worker protocol is unchanged (it claims in its own lane copy as before, and the line-level collision resolves under last-writer-wins). Test spec: integration test in tests/br_roundtrip.rs — temp workspace with one ready bead, run the abacus binary with PATH restricted so br resolves but herdr does not; expect non-zero exit at the herdr leg AND the bead now in_progress in the temp store, proving the claim precedes lane creation. Unit-level: none needed beyond existing selection tests; the claim is a shell-out.

title: Dispatch race: prompt sent before codex owns the terminal is lost, agent_prompt_stalled
description: Observed dispatch 6, 2026-08-13 17:56: abacus run selected ab-s1x, opened lane w1X, herdr agent start returned success, but herdr agent prompt --wait failed with agent_prompt_stalled (no state change in 5000ms, status idle). Forensics from the standing lane: the dispatch prompt text is rendered ABOVE the codex banner in the pane transcript — it was typed into the terminal before the codex TUI attached, so codex started with an empty composer and never saw the prompt (context 0 percent, placeholder visible). Dispatch 5 ran the identical sequence successfully — this is a startup race, not a deterministic break. The engine correctly exited 1 without probe or reap, leaving the lane standing. Fix shape, evidence-gated per MVP-first: in cmd_run (src/main.rs), on an agent prompt failure whose stderr contains agent_prompt_stalled, retry the identical herdr agent prompt --wait once — a re-prompt into an idle empty composer is exactly what recovered run 1 manually and is idempotent; if the retry also stalls, fail as now and leave the lane for forensics. Test spec: unit test the stalled-detection predicate on the captured error string; the retry leg is validated live and recorded in notes. Captured error, verbatim: agent prompt produced no observed state change within 5000 ms; status is idle and state_change_seq remained 1578.
close_reason: Done by codex lane, commit d0a26f2 on lane/ab-lpk (pushed, engine auto-verified and auto-reaped; all 6 suites rerun green by orchestrator from the branch). Retry-once on agent_prompt_stalled.

title: git merge driver for .beads/issues.jsonl: last-writer-wins per issue line
description: Two real conflicts on 2026-08-13 (PR 2 and PR 3) from lane close commits colliding with a moving main tracker, and br sync --import-only rejects files containing conflict markers outright, so an unresolved merge also bricks the tracker. Implement an abacus merge-jsonl <ours> <base> <theirs> subcommand in src/main.rs: parse each side as JSONL keyed by issue id; for ids present on both sides emit the line with the later updated_at; union ids present on one side only; write the result over the ours path and exit 0; any parse failure exits non-zero so git falls back to a normal conflict for manual resolution. Wire-up: commit a .gitattributes line mapping .beads/issues.jsonl to merge=beads-jsonl, and document the per-clone git config for merge.beads-jsonl.driver (abacus merge-jsonl %A %O %B) in AGENTS.md — gotcha: git config is per-clone and cannot be committed, only .gitattributes can. The resolution rule is proven: applied by hand on PR 2 (three contested bead lines, main side newer on all) and PR 3. Test spec: unit tests for the three-way merge function (same id both sides newer-wins by updated_at; disjoint ids union; malformed line errors); integration test constructing base/ours/theirs fixture files, running the subcommand via CARGO_BIN_EXE, asserting merged output and exit codes; live git-level validation on the next lane merge recorded in bead notes.
notes: LIVE VALIDATION 2026-08-13 evening: first real merge with the driver active (lane/ab-lpk merging origin/main, both sides touching the ab-lpk line) auto-resolved cleanly — Auto-merging .beads/issues.jsonl, ort strategy, no conflict — and the surviving line was main's newer close as intended. Six suites green on the merged tree. Driver configured per-clone in the operator checkout; abacus installed to ~/.cargo/bin so git can invoke it.

title: Dot-numbered bead ids are invalid herdr agent names; dispatch dies at agent start
description:
Observed 2026-08-14 08:52, first dispatch of an epic child: abacus run
selected ab-qmc.1, opened the worktree lane successfully (herdr sanitizes
the checkout path itself), then herdr agent start ab-qmc.1 failed with
error code invalid_agent_name — the name grammar allows only a lowercase
first letter and lowercase letters, digits, hyphen, or underscore, 1-32
characters. Epic children minted by br carry dotted ids (parent.N), so
every epic child dispatch dies at the agent-start leg. The engine exited 1
and left the lane standing, which was correct.

Fix in src/main.rs cmd_run: derive the agent name from the bead id by
replacing every character outside the allowed grammar with a hyphen (and
truncating to 32 characters), then use that sanitized name consistently for
herdr agent start and herdr agent prompt. The bead id itself stays exact in
the branch name, the dispatch prompt text, and the outcome probe — identity
carriage is untouched; only the herdr display name is sanitized.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an epic and a child in br (child id becomes parent.1).
2. Make the child the highest-priority ready bead.
3. abacus run: worktree create succeeds, agent start fails with
   invalid_agent_name, exit 1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A sanitize function maps any bead id to a valid herdr agent name
  (allowed grammar, max 32 chars) and is unit-tested on dotted ids,
  uppercase, and over-length inputs.
- cmd_run uses the sanitized name for agent start and agent prompt; branch,
  prompt text, and outcome probe keep the exact bead id.
- Full suite, clippy, fmt green; live validation is the next epic-child
  dispatch, recorded in notes.
notes: Root cause confirmed: cmd_run reused the exact bead id as Herdr's display/routing name even though dotted child ids violate Herdr's grammar. Red-first evidence: cargo test --test br_roundtrip abacus_run_sanitizes_only_the_herdr_name_for_a_dotted_child_id -- --exact --nocapture failed before implementation because raw child id it-j7h.1 reached herdr agent start and the protocol fake returned invalid_agent_name. Green evidence: sanitizer unit regression 1/1 passed; dotted-child command integration regression 1/1 passed; full cargo test passed 14 lib, 3 bin, 10 br_roundtrip, 2 merge_jsonl, and 2 version tests, with doc tests also green; cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings passed; cargo fmt --check passed. The next real epic-child dispatch is the live validation: confirm agent start and prompt route through the hyphenated name while branch, dispatch prompt text, and br outcome probe retain the exact dotted bead id.

title: Worker opens the PR itself: dispatch protocol ends at gh pr create
description: Currently the worker protocol in dispatch_prompt (src/lib.rs) ends at push plus br close, and the orchestrator opens PRs by hand — PRs 1 through 4 were all manual gh pr create calls. Per NORTH-STAR.md the lane's deliverable is a PR ready for operator review, so the worker should produce it. Change dispatch_prompt so the protocol order becomes: br close <id>, stage .beads, commit, git push -u origin <branch>, then gh pr create --base main with a title carrying the bead id and a body summarizing what was done and the test evidence (suite results, red-first confirmation). gh is authenticated machine-wide. Tolerance: if a PR already exists for the branch (re-dispatch of an incomplete lane), gh pr create fails — instruct the worker to treat an existing PR for its branch as success rather than a blocker. Do not mandate any attribution footer; the worker writes its own body. Test spec: update the dispatch_prompt unit test in src/lib.rs to assert gh pr create appears in the prompt and appears after the push instruction; live validation is the next dispatched lane ending with a PR URL in its transcript, recorded in this bead's notes on close. Gotcha for the implementing lane: this bead itself edits dispatch_prompt, the same function ab-iuf's claim change sits near in main.rs flow — sequential dispatch, no shared-file concurrency.
close_reason: Done by codex lane, commit 53eee2f on lane/ab-yil (pushed, engine auto-verified and auto-reaped; six suites rerun green by orchestrator). Dispatch protocol now ends at gh pr create; live validation is the next dispatched lane.

title: Codex first-run hooks-trust modal blocks dispatched lanes
description: Reproduced live 2026-08-13, first dispatch of abacus run (see abacus-geh notes). A codex agent started by herdr agent start --kind codex in a fresh worktree lane (~/.herdr/worktrees/abacus/lane-abacus-v8s) presents an interactive review modal on startup: 3 hooks need review before they can run, Press t to trust all (2 PreToolUse, 1 SessionStart — the operator's own kept hooks from ~/.codex config). The dispatched prompt is never processed; the lane does zero work. Repro: herdr worktree create on this repo, herdr agent start x --kind codex --pane <pane>, herdr agent read x — the modal is on screen. Investigation directions, evidence-gated per MVP-first: find where codex stores hook trust (global vs per-directory — if per-directory, every fresh worktree will hit this) and whether a config flag or codex exec style non-interactive invocation bypasses the modal for already-operator-approved hooks. The fix belongs in how abacus (or herdr agent start) launches codex, not in removing the hooks.
acceptance_criteria: A freshly created worktree lane started with herdr agent start --kind codex reaches the composer with hooks active and processes its dispatch prompt without any interactive keypress. Verified by dispatching a trivial bead through abacus run end to end with no manual send-keys.
notes: RESOLVED BY EVIDENCE, 2026-08-13 evening. Probe: fresh worktree lane (w1R, branch lane/probe-5pe), herdr agent start --kind codex — codex v0.147.0 reached its composer directly, no modal. Mechanism found: codex stores hook trust in ~/.codex/config.toml under [hooks.state], one entry per hook keyed by source path + event + index, holding a sha256 trusted_hash of the hook content. Scope is GLOBAL and content-addressed, not per-directory: the single manual trust-all during run 1 of abacus-geh covered all future lanes. The run-1 modal was the one-time first-run review of the operator's kept hooks after the SABLE hook removal reshuffled configs. Recurrence condition: any hook content change or new hook re-triggers one global review modal, and a lane dispatched in that window stalls exactly like run 1 — detection of that is abacus-zkq's outcome probe, which is the correct layer; no launch-path change in abacus is warranted. Acceptance verified live: dispatch 2 (lane w1S, bead abacus-zkq) went end to end with no manual keypress — prompt received and worker running. Probe lane fully torn down.
close_reason: No engine change warranted: hook trust is global and content-addressed in ~/.codex/config.toml [hooks.state]; the one-time operator trust covers all lanes. Recurrence (hook content change) stalls a lane detectably — that detection is abacus-zkq scope.

title: AGENTS.md: one-page worker orientation
description: Write a one-page AGENTS.md at the repo root orienting any agent landing in this repository: NORTH-STAR.md is the standard every proposal is judged against; CONSTRAINTS.md carries the measured findings (read it); work state lives in br (br ready, br show <id>, br update <id> --claim, br close <id>); lanes are git worktrees under ~/.herdr/worktrees/abacus/ on branches named lane/<bead-id>; workers self-push their lane branch; autonomy ends at the PR — no merging to main. Keep it to one page; link, do not restate. Docs-only change, [no-test].

title: abacus run: single-pass dispatch skeleton
description: Build a cargo bin crate named abacus at the repo root exposing the subcommand run. Single pass, no loop: shell out to br ready --json in the target repo (default: current directory), take the first ready bead, shell herdr worktree create --cwd <repo> --branch lane/<bead-id> --no-focus and parse the JSON result for the new workspace and pane ids, then herdr agent start <bead-id> --kind codex --pane <pane-id>, then herdr agent prompt <name> <dispatch-text> --wait, and print the settled state. The dispatch text must carry the bead id and instruct the worker to run br show <bead-id> for its scope. Shelling out is the design, per SHIFT-REPORT-2026-08-13 section 3: records, acceptance, and evidence chains are explicitly out of scope. Measured finding 3 from the report applies: the launch must carry the bead identity (branch name plus prompt text is the MVP carriage). Test spec: unit tests in src for parsing br ready JSON from a fixture string; integration test that runs real br init plus br create plus br ready --json in a temp dir and exercises the selection code against it. The herdr leg is validated by a live dogfood dispatch, recorded in the bead notes on close.
notes: Landed in commit after 88903b7 (feat: abacus run skeleton). Gates: cargo test 13/13 green (9 unit, 4 integration with real br in temp workspaces and the real binary via CARGO_BIN_EXE), clippy clean, fmt clean. The herdr parse leg is tested against a JSON fixture captured from a live herdr worktree create probe; the live end-to-end herdr leg is deliberately abacus-geh scope, which this bead unblocks. Selection semantics decided during build: lowest priority number wins, ties keep br output order. Dispatch prompt carries bead id and branch (finding 3 MVP carriage) plus the worker protocol: claim, test-first, push lane branch, br close.

title: abacus --version flag prints crate version
description: Add a --version (and -V) flag to the abacus binary that prints abacus plus the crate version from Cargo.toml (use the CARGO_PKG_VERSION env macro) and exits 0. The crate lives at the repo root, src/main.rs parses args by hand (no clap) — follow the existing arg-handling style. Deliberately small: this bead is the designated dispatch target for the first live abacus run (see the first-live-dispatch bead), so a worker lane can prove the full loop on it. Test spec: unit test asserting the version string function returns the CARGO_PKG_VERSION value; integration test in tests/ running the built binary with --version via std::process::Command and asserting stdout contains the version and exit code 0. Write the failing test first, then implement. Commit on the lane branch, push it, close this bead.

title: CONSTRAINTS.md: carry the four measured findings
description: Write CONSTRAINTS.md at the repo root carrying the four measured findings from SHIFT-REPORT-2026-08-13-CLAUDE.md section 7, substance intact: (1) br not bd — at 11 concurrent claimants br served 879 reads with zero timeouts (p50 51ms) while bd recorded 15/15 read timeouts at similar width; (2) provider identity must bind to every execution, not startup — a cached verdict, a held inode, and an ambient staging root each defeated a naive gate, all three reproduced live; (3) the worker launch environment must carry bead and attempt, or a context-lost worker cannot enumerate its own records; (4) crash recovery is first-class on this host — the operator machine crashes, and requires-a-crash-at-the-wrong-moment is not a mitigating argument. title: abacus run never reaps the lane: worker pane and workspace persist after completion
description: Observed on the first live dispatch (abacus-geh, 2026-08-13): after the codex worker on lane/abacus-v8s finished and its work was verified and the bead closed, the lane workspace w1P, its worktree checkout, and the idle codex pane persisted indefinitely — the operator had to point it out. At ten concurrent lanes this leaks ten workspaces, ten worktrees, and ten idle agent panes per pass. Fix shape: after the post-settle outcome probe (abacus-zkq introduces it), a verified-complete lane (bead closed) is torn down with herdr worktree remove --workspace <id> — the Lane struct in src/lib.rs already carries workspace_id. The pushed lane branch is the surviving artifact and is never deleted. A lane that did NOT complete (bead open or in_progress) is deliberately left standing for forensics — the pane transcript is the evidence and dies with the pane. Note worktree remove may need --force when the lane holds uncommitted .beads changes, which is currently always per abacus-zyb; the first lane (w1P) was reaped manually with force for exactly this reason. Test spec: unit test the reap decision from the outcome classification (closed reaps, open and in_progress do not); the herdr teardown call is validated live on the next dispatched lane and recorded in notes. Needs abacus-zkq (the outcome probe is what makes reaping safe to decide).
notes: Deferred 2026-08-13: tracker dep (zkq closed) is satisfied, but the code this bead builds on — the post-settle outcome probe — lives only on unmerged lane/abacus-zkq. A lane dispatched for wrq would branch from main and find nothing to hook into. Undefer when the operator merges lane/abacus-zkq to main; the tomorrow date is a re-check tick, not the real condition.

title: abacus run cannot tell a gated lane from a finished one
description: Reproduced live 2026-08-13, first dispatch (see abacus-geh notes). herdr agent prompt --wait settled with agent_status done while the codex worker was actually parked on a startup modal and had processed nothing: no claim on the bead, no commit, no push. abacus run printed the settle JSON and exited 0 — a false success. The settle state alone is not evidence of work. Cheapest evidence-based check per MVP-first, in src/main.rs cmd_run after settle: shell br show <bead-id> --json in the lane checkout (the Lane struct already carries checkout_path) and report the bead status the worker left behind — closed means done, in_progress means it worked but did not finish, still open means the worker never engaged (exit non-zero and say so). Do not build state-machine heuristics over herdr agent states; one br probe distinguishes the three outcomes that matter. Test spec: unit test the outcome classification from bead status; integration test the open-bead path with a fake lane dir holding an initialized br workspace. Needs abacus-5pe understood first only if the fix shape ends up in the launch path; the report-what-the-bead-says probe stands alone.
acceptance_criteria: After settle, abacus run probes br show <bead-id> --json in the lane checkout and reports the outcome from bead status: closed exits 0 as success, in_progress reports incomplete, open reports never-engaged, both non-zero. Unit test covers the three-way classification; integration test covers the open path with a real br workspace in a temp lane dir. Run-1 conditions (worker gated on a modal, settle says done) would exit non-zero.
notes: Corroboration, 2026-08-13: the abacus-v1 orchestrator hit the identical failure independently the same night (herdr done treated as completion while the agent was parked), and the sf reference implementation states the rule outright: either signal is a doorbell, not evidence. Three independent arrivals — this run, v1's, and sf's — make the failure structural, not incidental. The fix shape stands: probe br in the lane for the bead status; never treat runtime agent state as an outcome.

title: Dispatch prompt orders close after push, stranding bead state in the lane
description: Observed on the first successful lane (run 2 of abacus-geh, 2026-08-13). dispatch_prompt in src/lib.rs instructs the worker: commit, push with git push -u origin <branch>, then br close <id>. The close therefore mutates the lane's .beads/issues.jsonl AFTER the branch is pushed, leaving the closed status as an uncommitted working-tree change in the worktree — the pushed branch carries the bead as open, and the main checkout's tracker learns nothing. The codex worker on lane/abacus-v8s reported exactly this: only uncommitted change is .beads/issues.jsonl, produced by the requested post-push br close. Fix shape: reorder the protocol in dispatch_prompt to close the bead before the final commit+push so the branch carries its own completion record (br close, then git add .beads, commit, push). Update the dispatch_prompt unit test in src/lib.rs to assert the ordering (close appears before push in the prompt text). Note the residual gap is claim/close visibility across live lanes generally — that is the known no-tree-claim-coordination hazard, out of scope here; this bead only stops the protocol from stranding state by construction.
acceptance_criteria: dispatch_prompt orders the protocol as br close, then commit including .beads, then push — the pushed lane branch carries the bead closed status. The dispatch_prompt unit test asserts close appears before push in the prompt text. A dispatched lane leaves no uncommitted .beads changes after settling.
notes: Run-3 evidence (zkq lane): the codex worker improvised the correct behavior unprompted — after the instructed push it closed the bead, committed the jsonl as a second commit (7672d49 tracker: close abacus-zkq), and pushed again, so the branch carried its close and the lane reaped with no force. The bead remains valid: the protocol should make this deterministic in dispatch_prompt rather than worker-dependent improvisation. Also note the reap contrast: v8s lane (no close commit) required forced removal; zkq lane (close committed) removed clean.
